A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bulk-calibrated credal ambiguity-set framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A-H are readable and support reliable matching across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original newsvendor simulations, California housing regression results, CivilComments classification results, and supplementary empirical analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds baseline comparisons, convergence diagnostics, and sensitivity and ablation results.

M1.justification: The forward-LV mean-plus-sup objective, DKW bulk calibration, centre choices, and LV-Group discounting procedure are retained. The new geometry, smoothing, and classifier-head experiments evaluate variants of the existing framework without revising its proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same newsvendor demand distributions and contamination levels, California East-West geographic scenarios, CivilComments task and populations, and illustrative bulk-calibration distributions. Added experiments vary configurations within this retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds KL-DRO and chi-square DRO to the housing CV, runtime, oracle, and sweep comparisons (Tables 7-9 and Figure 12). Figure 16 adds bulk-filtered ERM, CVaR, and chi-square DRO controls to CivilComments; GroupDRO-B already appeared in v1. These extend the retained comparator sets.

E3.justification: Main splits, metrics, sampling budgets, and selection procedures remain unchanged. New supplementary protocols measure normalized SAA error, sweep gamma from 0.043 to 0.15, evaluate a housing box bulk set, and test CivilComments bulk-filtered controls, smoothmax temperature 0.01, and a width-256 MLP head.

E4.justification: Appendices F-H substantially expand checks of the framework's approximations and design choices: rejection-sampling convergence, tail-budget sensitivity, box versus product bulk geometry, filtering effects across baselines, sharper smoothmax, and a nonlinear classifier head. The 8192-feature experiment was already in v1 and is retained as Figure 18b.

E5.justification: Both versions report 100 replications for newsvendor and housing, 20 for the main CivilComments comparison, mean/SD summaries, and 95% newsvendor confidence bands. The new convergence diagnostic uses the existing 100-replication, 95% uncertainty-reporting practice; no increased run counts or new statistical testing procedure is reported.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for the new comparisons and diagnostics. Housing LV MAE changes from 10.6 to 10.7 in units of 10000, and total runtime from 1.58 to 1.44 seconds (Tables 3-4). Main CivilComments scores remain unchanged. The new MLP comparison reports LV-Group/GroupDRO worst-group accuracies of 0.485/0.425, with mean accuracies of 0.829/0.856.

T1.justification: Corollary 2.2 now explicitly assumes epsilon > 0 and separates the singleton ambiguity set at epsilon = 0, correcting the earlier unrestricted non-attainment statement. Appendix B.1 also handles this edge case explicitly. The principal risk certificate, calibration guarantees, and existing appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions retain the same scientific scope: finite, tractable bulk-restricted contamination objectives, calibration and risk guarantees, the IP-DRO connection, and favorable empirical robustness and computation. Reordering the contribution list and adding supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies Theorem 3.4 as a structural decomposition when deployment quantities are unobservable. Appendix F.8 adds explanations and practical recommendations for gamma-related instability and excessive truncation. Appendix G.7 interprets box-bulk instability through changes between extreme-point solutions, extending the existing geometry discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds a reproduction-code link, identifies the Python DRO package for the added housing baselines, and specifies settings for new ablations. Existing software and hardware disclosures remain. However, v1's explicit list of CV-selected housing parameters in Appendix G.4 is omitted from the corresponding v2 section.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on imprecise probability, convex support functions, DRO software, and online conformal prediction, including an online-calibration future-work connection. It removes the Donsker-Varadhan citation and replaces the PyTorch reference. The central positioning relative to contamination models and divergence-ball DRO remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds subsections within Sections 2 and 5.2, introduces roadmaps and reorganizes settings and results in Appendices F-H, standardizes loss notation, and updates editorial and publication text. The main narrative sequence and most theoretical exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially: v2 adds the centre/SAA summary table, extended housing tables, and convergence, sensitivity, geometry, filtering, smoothing, and MLP plots. Housing sweep plots gain comparator curves. The existing 8192-feature figure is combined with the new MLP panel, and several legends, labels, and display placements are revised.

improvement.justification: The additional controls and sensitivity analyses in Appendices F-H strengthen validation and provide useful guidance for the existing framework. The epsilon-zero correction, explicit certificate qualification, and reproduction-code link improve precision and usability. These are incremental gains over an already substantial study; omitting the previously listed selected housing hyperparameters slightly reduces standalone reproducibility.
